**Triage** — graded, `finding` cleared. Re-measured at `origin/main` `ed44512`; both surviving copies are still there, verbatim.

## Confirmed

1. `scripts/check-regen-pending.mjs:413-415`, inside the `refuse-stale` branch itself:
   > Landing a merge? `bash scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` runs the sanctioned sequence — it commits the merge first (this hook records that as a deferral) and regeneration follows as its own commit.
2. `.githooks/pre-commit:12-14` — "That commit records a deferral instead of being refused; the immediately following commit must discharge it", with the true caveat at `:16-19` six lines below in the same header.

The self-contradiction in (2) is exactly as the card describes: the file asserts both that step 3 records a deferral and that a clean auto-committed merge lands with the marker untouched so "the refusal falls on the next commit". Only the second is measured.

## Your serial dependency is already discharged

The card asks for this to run "serial after PR #14468 lands". **It has landed** — `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh:110-115` on `ed44512` now reads

> Ruled 2026-08-12 (#8047): the hook gained a DEFERRAL mode — … ORDINARY commit — the hook's `refuse-stale` path, not its deferral path …

so the reference wording the card wants to copy exists in the tree today, at `os-regen-merge.sh:110-115`. Nothing blocks this card. No `Blocked-by:` line owed.

## Scope ruled — as the card proposes, unchanged

Two files, prose only: the `refuse-stale` message text (`check-regen-pending.mjs:413-415`) and the hook header (`.githooks/pre-commit:9-14`). State precisely that the deferral mode applies only to a merge finished by hand with `MERGE_HEAD` present at commit time, and that the script's step-3 commit is an ordinary commit whose refusal is the designed collection point. ⛔ No change to `decide()`, no bypass, no re-litigation of the hook's behaviour — #14154's triage already ruled the behaviour correct and this card inherits that. `scripts/**` ⇒ `skip-changeset`, per the convention PR #14468 followed.

The two spans the card explicitly did not read (`os-regen-merge.sh:32-99`, `.githooks/pre-push`) stay out of scope; if the implementer trips over the same sentence there, file it, do not widen.

## Routing

`domain:devx` — `scripts/**` gate code plus `.githooks/`; the SUBJECT here is regeneration-artifact hygiene, i.e. code/doc quality, not the governed agent-instruction surface, so it stays devx and does not cross into `domain:skills` (lane-table split by SUBJECT). `tooling` kept.

`priority:p2`, one step above the two prose cards graded alongside it this round (#14516, #14473, both p3). Those are passive staleness a reader may never hit. This one is printed **inside the refusal**, to an operator who is blocked at that moment, and it recommends the very command that produced the block. That is active misdirection at a stopping point, and the project has already paid once to fix the same sentence in a sibling file — leaving two copies standing is why it came back.

`pm:queue`.

No other in-flight card of this seat touches either file. Changeset: `scripts/**` + `.githooks/` ⇒ no changeset, `skip-changeset` label (the convention PR #14468 followed).
